subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve this as a narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated flag, or fold elevated authority into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The choice changes the trust boundary for elevated host exec across persisted cron jobs, agent-created schedules, heartbeat files/config, execution receipts, and upgrade behavior, which automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader Gateway-owned scheduling provenance design and keep heartbeat provenance explicitly in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now, with migration and tests for create, update, and execution-time checks.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove wildcard cron-event and heartbeat elevated inheritance unless maintainers intentionally preserve a separate compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader Gateway-owned scheduling provenance design and keep heartbeat provenance explicitly in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: PR #96883 is the nearest merged scheduling-provenance work and makes joshavant the clearest current routing owner for cron authority design.
